title: Adhesives
headline:
THE RIGHT BOND
STARTS WITH THE APPLICATION.
summary: Adhesive solutions for construction, manufacturing and industrial assembly.
heading: Bonding across different materials.
body: NAPCO develops adhesives for industrial, manufacturing and construction applications. Its published range includes hot-melt, instant and pressure-sensitive adhesives, thread-lockers and structural adhesives.

Acrylic, epoxy and urethane technologies are among the chemistries described in NAPCO’s portfolio. Selection should be tied to the materials, assembly process and requirements of the finished application.

FOCUS ON
THE JOINT.

The published portfolio is developed through consultation with customers and people involved in application. Discuss the joint, materials and operating conditions with NAPCO before choosing a product.

title: Coatings
headline:

THE SURFACE.

heading: Protection begins with the surface.
body: NAPCO’s coating portfolio covers construction and industrial applications. Its published examples include building panels, roofs, concrete floors and walls, HVAC, furniture and commercial appliances.
Research and development considers production requirements alongside the needs of the finished surface. Discuss the substrate, intended use and relevant product data with the technical team.

title: Construction solutions

BIG IDEAS.

heading: Build. Protect. Finish. Repair.
body: NAPCO’s construction offer is organised around four stages: Build, Protect, Finish and Repair. Its published applications include preparing, bonding, sealing and protecting building materials.

The current construction overview describes moisture-related applications, including foundations and basement damp-proofing. Use current technical information to establish the appropriate product and system for the project.

The relevant solution depends on the component and the production requirement. Bring the materials, application process and end-use conditions into the technical conversation.

Application requirements differ between components and devices. Discuss the assembly and the relevant chemical, mechanical and electrical conditions before selecting a formulation.

Start with the materials being joined and how the pack will be made and used. Any application with additional regulatory requirements needs product-specific confirmation.

title: Furniture & building components
headline:
CRAFT MEETS
CHEMISTRY.
summary: Bonding solutions for furniture and building components.
heading: From materials to the finished component.
body: NAPCO’s published furniture and building-components applications include edge banding, profile wrapping, flat lamination, wood assembly, edge sealing, sandwich-panel lamination and foam bonding.
Wood, MDF and other materials each bring different requirements. Start with the component and manufacturing process, then review the appropriate adhesive and its current documentation.

HOW YOU MAKE.

heading: Connect materials with the process.

The role of a material needs to be considered within the production process and the finished assembly. Discuss the substrates, operating conditions and product-specific requirements with NAPCO.

title: About NAPCO
headline:
WE MAKE
IT STICK!
summary: Adhesives, sealants and coatings for construction and industry.
heading: Consistent quality through innovation.
body: NAPCO combines adhesives, sealants and coatings with technical and research-and-development expertise. Its published applications span construction and industrial markets.

The company’s approach centres on understanding customer requirements and developing application-led solutions. The portfolio reaches across sectors including automotive, electronics, packaging, furniture and manufacturing.

title: Innovation strategy
headline:
TECHNICAL THINKING.
PRACTICAL RELEVANCE.
summary: A materials-focused approach to customer application challenges.
heading: Innovation starts with a real requirement.
body: NAPCO describes its innovation strategy as centred on material science. Its research and development work addresses functional materials, polymer building blocks and adhesive-bonding processes.

The published strategy also identifies reverse engineering as part of its technical approach. Customer requirements help frame the development of adhesives, coatings and sealants for the markets NAPCO serves.
